title: Chapter 2: The Story of the Merchant and the Jinnee
chineseTitle: 第 2 章：商人与巨精的故事

paragraphs.en: On her first night, Scheherazade began the story of a rich Merchant who sat down under a palm tree to eat dates, throwing the date stones right and left. Suddenly, a giant Jinnee of monstrous size appeared before him with a drawn sword, roaring: 'Rise, that I may kill thee with this sword, as thou hast killed my son!' The merchant cried out: 'How could I have killed your son?' 'When thou didst throw away date stones,' replied the Jinnee, 'one struck my son in the eye and killed him instantly.'
paragraphs.zh: 在她入宫的第一夜，雪赫拉查德开始讲述一个富商的故事，他坐在棕榈树下吃椰枣，左右乱扔枣核。突然，一个体型巨大的巨精手里举着拔出的剑出现在他面前，咆哮道：“站起来，以便我用这把剑杀死你，就像你杀死了我的儿子一样！”商人喊道：“我怎么可能杀了你的儿子？”“当你扔掉枣核时，”巨精回答，“其中一颗打中了我的儿子的眼睛，立刻要了他的命。”

paragraphs.en: The poor merchant begged for mercy, asking for a one-year reprieve to settle his affairs, distribute his wealth among his wife and children, and return to meet his death. Moved by the merchant's absolute honesty, the Jinnee granted his request. One year later, the faithful merchant returned to the palm tree, awaiting his doom. Three old men passed by, and hearing the merchant's tale, offered to tell the Jinnee three marvelous stories in exchange for his life. The Jinnee was so amazed by their tales that he spared the honest merchant.
paragraphs.zh: 可怜的商人恳求慈悲，要求一年的缓刑来处理他的事务，在妻子和孩子们中间分发财产，并回来接受死亡。被商人绝对的诚实所打动，巨精满足了他的请求。一年后，忠诚的商人回到了棕榈树下，等待着他的厄运。三个老人经过，听到商人的故事，提出向巨精讲述三个神奇的故事来换取他的生命。巨精被他们的故事所震撼，饶了这位诚实的商人。
